units.text: The Newmark permanent displacement $D_{n}$ quantifies the displacement induced by an earthquake accumulates in the sliding mass and is the performance measure from which the seismic coefficients are derived. The $D_{n}(k_{y})$ curves relate, for each combination of geometry, material, and design scenario, the yield acceleration $k_{y}$ to the expected permanent displacement; they were computed with an ensemble set of AM88 (Ambraseys & Menu, 1988), JB07 (Jibson, 2007), SR08 (Saygili & Rathje, 2008), BT07 (Bray & Travasarou, 2007), and BM19 (Bray & Macedo, 2019), with reference magnitudes $M_{w}$ = 5.5 and $M_{w}$ = 6.5 assigned according to the seismic demand and 300 realizations per demand and are read at the fractiles $q = 1 - p_{e}$. The horizontal pseudostatic coefficient $k_{h}$ is in turn derived from the allowable permanent displacement $D_{a}$ of the potentially sliding mass (Bray & Travasarou, Pseudostatic Coefficient for Use in Simplified Seismic Slope Stability Evaluation, 2009; Macedo, Bray, Abrahamson, & Travasarou, 2018); the coefficients are reported at four relative displacement limits, $D_{a}/H_{s}$ = 0.1, 0.4, 1.0, 2.5%, and the tables in Section **10.3** and **Appendix E** report, for the demands and scenarios analyzed, the coefficient at each limit, expressed as a percentage of the PGA.

contribution.evidence: Sentence one defines displacement; sentence two identifies the ensemble, magnitudes and realizations; sentence three defines kh, the four thresholds and where the results are tabulated. The corrected BM19 citation connects that model to its actual source.

Within each demand, that magnitude is common to the geometry, material and site combinations evaluated. The published form of each formulation is reproduced in **Appendix E**. units.text: The seismic-coefficient section applies five Newmark permanent-displacement formulations: three rigid-block models, two flexible-block models and, among the latter, the BM branch selected by the tectonic control of the project. This section reproduces the published form of each formulation, including both BM branches, and states the rule that defines the active configuration. The rigid-block formulations relate the displacement to measures of the base excitation, whereas the flexible-block formulations additionally incorporate the dynamic response of the sliding mass through its fundamental period $\mathbf{T}_{\mathbf{s}}$ and the spectral acceleration evaluated at a period proportional to $\mathbf{T}_{\mathbf{s}}$.

contribution.evidence: Sentence one distinguishes three rigid and two flexible active models; sentence two explains why both BM equations are displayed; sentence three identifies the extra Ts/spectral predictor in flexible models. All three are needed to read the formula list without treating both BM branches as active.

scope.evidence: Five active formulations, with one BM branch selected by tectonic context.

findings.fragment: Seismic coefficients for the Crawford project embankments were estimated using an empirical
findings.diagnosis: The singular empirical-method summary does not describe the active ensemble.

resolution.evidence: Full report executive paragraph copied; ensemble, demand allocation and sample count retained.
resolution.replacement: The Newmark permanent displacement $D_{n}$ quantifies the displacement induced by an earthquake and accumulated in the sliding mass and is the performance measure from which the seismic coefficients are derived. The $D_{n}(k_{y})$ curves relate, for each combination of geometry, material, and design scenario, the yield acceleration $k_{y}$ to the expected permanent displacement; they were computed with the ensemble set of AM88, JB07, SR08, BT07, and BM19, with the reference magnitude assigned to each seismic demand and 300 realizations per demand and are read at the fractiles $q = 1 - p_{e}$.
